defect: The stiffness contribution is built from the parametric gradients basisGrads instead of the physical gradients basisPhGrads, so the geometry map is ignored.
The stiffness visitor builds the local matrix from the parametric gradients (basisGrads) instead of the physical gradients (basisPhGrads) it has just computed.

The two new addCornerValue overloads (int p, boxCorner c, T v, int unk) and (boxCorner c, T v, int unk) are ambiguous for natural calls because boxCorner converts implicitly to/from integers and enums.

The overloads addCornerValue(int p, boxCorner c, T v, int u) and addCornerValue(boxCorner c, T v, int u) are ambiguous for normal 3-argument calls such as (0, boundary::southwest, 1.0) or (boundary::southwest, 0.0, 0), because boxCorner converts implicitly from int and from boundary::corner.

defect: slice() names gsTensorBSpline<d-1,T>. The same commit adds explicit full-class instantiations for d=1, so gsTensorBSpline<0,T> gets instantiated and the build fails.
slice() names gsTensorBSpline<d-1,T> and gsTensorBSplineBasis<d-1,...>. This commit also explicitly instantiates gsTensorBSpline<1,...>, so d drops to 0 and the build fails.

clear() now resets m_dim=-1 and nboxes=0, but gsMultiPatch::computeTopology calls clear() and then uses m_dim (1<<m_dim) and the box count.
BoundaryGeometryType and BoundaryBasisType are hard-coded to dimension 1 instead of d-1, which is wrong for d != 2 and breaks slice/boundary for 3D.
BoundaryGeometryType and BoundaryBasisType are hard-coded to dimension 1 instead of d-1, so slice() is wrong (fails to compile) for d != 2.

The new breakPolylineIntoTwoParts uses the alternative token `and` (`!p1 and !p2`), which MSVC rejects by default, so the build fails on Windows.
jacobian_into reshapes the deriv_into output (layout c*parDim+j per point) to tarDim rows and block-transposes with domainDim(), which scrambles the Jacobian whenever domainDim != targetDim.
jacobian_into reshapes the derivative matrix to tarDim rows and block-transposes by domainDim. The derivative data is stored as domainDim x tarDim blocks, so non-square Jacobians come out wrong.
clone() passes *piece(i).clone() to addPiece, which clones again, so every intermediate clone leaks.
clone() calls addPiece(*piece(i).clone()), but addPiece clones its argument again, so every temporary clone leaks.

defect: gaussSeidelSingleBlock builds the diagonal block as A.block(DoFs(i), DoFs(i)-i, 1, size), which is only correct for contiguous DoF blocks.

gaussSeidelSingleBlock builds the diagonal block as A.block(DoFs(i), DoFs(i)-i, 1, size), which is only correct when the block's DoFs are consecutive; for any other blocking the result is silently wrong.
The new degreeDecrease lowers m_p but calls increaseMultFirst/Last, copied from degreeIncrease, so it increases the end multiplicities instead of trimming them.
The new degreeDecrease lowers m_p but then calls increaseMultFirst/Last (copied from degreeIncrease) instead of reducing the end multiplicities.
The default active_into calls result.setConstant(0,u.cols()), with the arguments in the wrong order, instead of building a 1 x cols matrix of zeros.
The default active_into calls result.setConstant(0,u.cols()), which is Eigen's (size,value) form: it yields an empty matrix filled with u.cols() instead of a 1 x cols row of zeros.

defect: The new assertion `2*p+1 > sz` is inverted; a valid knot vector needs sz > 2p+1, so every valid construction fails it.
The assertion is inverted: `2*p+1 > sz` fires for every valid knot vector and accepts too-short ones.
insertKnot uses this->m_weights, which gsTensorNurbs does not have (weights live in the basis), and calls basis() helpers on the rational basis, so it does not compile when instantiated.

The new insertKnot uses this->m_weights (no such member in gsTensorNurbs; weights live in gsRationalBasis) and calls size_cwise/component on the rational basis, so it does not compile when instantiated.
The added return statement uses the nonexistent type gsMatrix<T>::uPt instead of uPtr, so the template fails to compile when instantiated.
The return statement this change added uses the nonexistent `gsMatrix<T>::uPt` instead of `uPtr`, so gsPointGrid fails to compile when instantiated.
The new point-count formula ceil(n*L_i/prod(L)) is only right for unit domains (e.g. [0,2]x[0,1] with 100 points gives 10x5=50 points).
The number of points per direction is computed as ceil(n/prod(L) * L_i) with n = N^(1/d), which is dimensionally wrong (for example L=(2,2), N=100 gives 5x5 instead of 10x10).

defect: The auto_ptr refactor added `typename` to the explicit-instantiation declarations, which are not templates (T is a macro for real_t), so they are ill-formed before C++11.

The explicit instantiation declarations (with T a macro, not a template parameter) use `typename gsGeometryEvaluator<T>::uPtr` and `typename gsBasis<T>::domainIter` outside a template, which is ill-formed in C++98.
apply1 clears m_elWise on each call, so a caller that loops over boundary sides keeps only the element values of the last side.
The new apply1 clears m_elWise on every call, so when gsNormL2Boundary calls it once per boundary side, the element-wise values from earlier sides are lost.
The quadrature rule reads options.getInt("quA"), but quA is registered as a Real option, so the lookup fails at runtime.
Reads the quadrature option with options.getInt("quA"), but quA is registered as a Real option, so the lookup fails at runtime.
BlockTranspose::coeff/packet compute the source row and column with m_numBlocks instead of m_matrix.rows() and rows(), so they read the wrong entries.
BlockTranspose::coeff and packet compute the source row and block from colId using m_numBlocks instead of m_matrix.rows(), so they read the wrong entries unless rows equal numBlocks.

The fallback for a missing MPI_IN_PLACE is written backwards: '#define inout MPI_IN_PLACE' defines the macro inout instead of MPI_IN_PLACE, while the code later #undefs MPI_IN_PLACE.
constructSolution now takes dim from solVector.cols(), so when there are no free dofs (an empty solution vector) dim is 0 and the coefficients get the wrong width.

constructSolution now takes dim = solVector.cols() instead of numRhs(), so when there are no free dofs (empty solution vector) dim is 0 and no coefficients, including the Dirichlet ones, are reconstructed.
std::free is called on the pointer returned by getenv, which the program does not own, so the call is undefined behaviour and can crash.
getTempPath calls std::free on the pointer returned by getenv, which is an invalid free and can corrupt the heap.
interpolateGrid now returns memory::unique_ptr but still does `return 0;` in the debug-only failure branch, which does not compile with the C++98 unique_ptr emulation (explicit constructor).
interpolateGrid now returns memory::unique_ptr, but the debug-only failure path still does `return 0;`, which does not compile with G+Smo's C++98 auto_ptr-based unique_ptr (explicit constructor).
The new templated pushSparse iterates a gsSparseMatrix<T> with gsSparseMatrix<double>::InnerIterator, so it fails to compile when T is not double.
The new pushSparse iterates gsSparseMatrix<T> localMat with gsSparseMatrix<double>::InnerIterator, which fails to compile for non-double T.

fix_subject: fix visitor dg related to multiple rhs
defect: The local rhs matrices are zeroed with a single column, which breaks system.push with eliminated DoFs when the system has several rhs columns.
localToGlobal pushes with local RHS blocks fixed at one column (setZero(rows,1)), which breaks systems with several right-hand-side columns.
In maxEigenvalue the ternaries mix T and int (`cond ? math::abs(..) : 0`), which fails to compile for non-double scalar types such as GMP/MPFR reals.
The ternaries `cond ? math::abs(m_gamma[i]) : 0` mix T and int, so they fail to compile for non-builtin coefficient types such as mpreal.
After switching to physBasisd2 from transformDeriv2Hgrad, the code still indexes it as physBasisd2(fct_i*d2_offsetter+j, k), but that result is numFuncs x numDers for a single point.
physBasisd2 from transformDeriv2Hgrad(k,...) is an N x d(d+1)/2 matrix for point k, but the code indexes it as physBasisd2(fct_i*d2_offsetter+m, k), the layout of basis2ndDerivs.

fix_subject: fix a small bug in gsBoxTopology.cpp (#302)
defect: allComponents indexes it->second[i] with the outer loop index instead of j, and never pushes 'last' into result.
In the combineCorners branch of allComponents, the loop pushes it->second[i] (the outer dimension index, always 0) instead of it->second[j], and the collected `last` vector is never added to result.
reshape_expr asserts on _u.rows()/cols() in the constructor before data exists, and eval returns a reshape map of the temporary returned by _u.eval(k), which dangles.
reshape_expr::eval returns a gsAsMatrix view (reshape) of the temporary from _u.eval(k), so the view dangles. The constructor also asserts on rows()*cols() before any data exists.

`reducedG1BasisEdgeMap[numG1EdgeBasis[i-1]] == 0 || i == 0` evaluates numG1EdgeBasis[i-1] with size_t i==0 (out of bounds) before the i==0 test. The i==0 branch also overwrites entries already set via an interface.
`if(reducedG1BasisEdgeMap[numG1EdgeBasis[i-1]] == 0 || i == 0)` evaluates numG1EdgeBasis[i-1] with i==0 (size_t underflow) before the i==0 test, so it reads out of bounds.
For surfaces, outerNormal crosses the tangent with the unnormalized normal t1 x t2, so the outer normal has the wrong magnitude, and the computed normalizedRes goes unused.

For surfaces, the outer normal is now signJk.cross(n) with the unnormalized normal n = t1 x t2, so its length is wrong (scaled by the area element). The normalized normal normalizedRes is still computed but left unused.

+/** @file gsLinpLapAssembler.h
+
+@brief Provides assembler for the linearized p-Laplace equation.
+
+This file is part of the G+Smo library.
+
+This Source Code Form is subject to the terms of the Mozilla Public
+License, v. 2.0. If a copy of the MPL was not distributed with this
+file, You can obtain one at http://mozilla.org/MPL/2.0/.
+
+Author(s): 
+*/
+
+#pragma once
+
+#include <gsAssembler/gsAssembler.h>
+#include <gsPde/gsLinpLapPde.h>
+
+#include <gsAssembler/gsVisitorLinpLap.h> // Stiffness volume integrals
+#include <gsAssembler/gsVisitorNeumann.h> // Neumann boundary integrals
+#include <gsAssembler/gsVisitorNitsche.h> // Nitsche boundary integrals
+#include <gsAssembler/gsVisitorDg.h>      // DG interface integrals
+
+
+namespace gismo
+{
+
+	/** @brief
+	Implementation of an (multiple right-hand side) linearized p-Laplace assembler.
+
+	The LinpLap equation: \f$-\Delta\mathbf{u}=\mathbf{f} \f$
+
+	It sets up an assembler and assembles the system patch wise and combines
+	the patch-local stiffness matrices into a global system by various methods
+	(see gismo::gsInterfaceStrategy). It can also enforce Dirichlet boundary
+	conditions in various ways (see gismo::gsDirichletStrategy).
+
+	\ingroup Assembler
+	*/
+	template <class T>
+	class gsLinpLapAssembler : public gsAssembler<T>
+	{
+	public:
+		typedef gsAssembler<T> Base;
+
+	public:
+
+		gsLinpLapAssembler()
+		{ }
+
+		/** @brief Main Constructor of the assembler object.
+
+		\param[in] pde A boundary value Poisson problem
+		\param[in] bases a multi-basis that contains patch-wise bases
+		*/
+		gsLinpLapAssembler(const gsLinpLapPde<T>          & pde,
+			const gsMultiBasis<T>          & bases)
+		{
+			Base::initialize(pde, bases, m_options);
+		}
+
+
+		/** @brief Main Constructor of the assembler object.
+
+		\param[in] pde A boundary value LinpLap problem
+		\param[in] bases a multi-basis that contains patch-wise bases
+		\param[in] dirStrategy option for the treatment of Dirichlet boundary
+		\param[in] intStrategy option for the treatment of patch interfaces
+		*/
+		gsLinpLapAssembler(const gsLinpLapPde<T>          & pde,
+			const gsMultiBasis<T>          & bases,
+			dirichlet::strategy           dirStrategy,
+			iFace::strategy               intStrategy = iFace::glue)
+		{
+			m_options.setInt("DirichletStrategy", dirStrategy);
+			m_options.setInt("InterfaceStrategy", intStrategy);
+
+			Base::initialize(pde, bases, m_options);
+		}
+
+		/** @brief
+		Constructor of the assembler object.
+
+		\param[in] patches is a gsMultiPatch object describing the geometry.
+		\param[in] basis a multi-basis that contains patch-wise bases
+		\param[in] bconditions is a gsBoundaryConditions object that holds all boundary conditions.
+		\param[in] rhs is the right-hand side of the linearized p-Laplace equation, \f$\mathbf{f}\f$.
+		\param[in] dirStrategy option for the treatment of Dirichlet boundary
+		\param[in] intStrategy option for the treatment of patch interfaces
+
+		\ingroup Assembler
+		*/
+		gsLinpLapAssembler(gsMultiPatch<T> const         & patches,
+			gsMultiBasis<T> const         & basis,
+			gsBoundaryConditions<T> const & bconditions,
+			const gsFunction<T>           & rhs,
+			const T &eps,
+			const T &p,
+			const gsMatrix<T> &w,
+			dirichlet::strategy           dirStrategy = dirichlet::elimination,
+			iFace::strategy               intStrategy = iFace::glue)
+		{
+			m_options.setInt("DirichletStrategy", dirStrategy);
+			m_options.setInt("InterfaceStrategy", intStrategy);
+
+			typename gsPde<T>::Ptr pde(new gsLinpLapPde<T>(patches, bconditions, rhs, eps, p, w))
+			Base::initialize(pde, basis, m_options);
+		}
+
+		virtual gsAssembler<T>* clone() const
+		{
+			return new gsLinpLapAssembler<T>(*this);
+		}
+
+		virtual gsAssembler<T>* create() const
+		{
+			return new gsLinpLapAssembler<T>();
+		}
+
+		// Refresh routine
+		virtual void refresh();
+
+		// Main assembly routine
+		virtual void assemble();
+
+		/// Returns an expression of the "full" assembled sparse
+		/// matrix. Note that matrix() might return a lower diagonal
+		/// matrix, if we exploit possible symmetry during assembly
+		/// (check: m_matrix.symmetry() == true )
+		Eigen::SparseSelfAdjointView< typename gsSparseMatrix<T>::Base, Lower> fullMatrix()
+		{
+			return m_system.matrix().template selfadjointView<Lower>();
+		}
+
+	protected:
+
+		// Members from gsAssembler
+		using Base::m_pde_ptr;
+		using Base::m_bases;
+		using Base::m_ddof;
+		using Base::m_options;
+		using Base::m_system;
+	};
+
+	template<class T>
+	void gsLinpLapAssembler<T>::refresh()
+	{
+		// We use predefined helper which initializes the system matrix
+		// rows and columns using the same test and trial space
+		Base::scalarProblemGalerkinRefresh();
+	}
+
+	template<class T>
+	void gsLinpLapAssembler<T>::assemble()
+	{
+		GISMO_ASSERT(m_system.initialized(),
+			"Sparse system is not initialized, call initialize() or refresh()");
+
+		// Reserve sparse system
+		m_system.reserve(m_bases[0], m_options, this->pde().numRhs());
+
+		// Compute the Dirichlet Degrees of freedom (if needed by m_options)
+		Base::computeDirichletDofs();
+
+		// Clean the sparse system
+		// m_system.setZero(); //<< this call leads to a quite significant performance degrade!
+
+		// Assemble volume integrals
+		Base::template push<gsVisitorLinpLap<T> >();
+
+		// Enforce Neumann boundary conditions
+		Base::template push<gsVisitorNeumann<T> >(m_pde_ptr->bc().neumannSides());
+
+		switch (m_options.getInt("DirichletStrategy"))
+		{
+		case dirichlet::penalize:
+			Base::penalizeDirichletDofs();
+			break;
+		case dirichlet::nitsche:
+			Base::template push<gsVisitorNitsche<T> >(m_pde_ptr->bc().dirichletSides());
+			break;
+		default:
+			break;
+		}
+
+		if (m_options.getInt("InterfaceStrategy") == iFace::dg)
+			Base::template pushInterface<gsVisitorDg<T> >();
+
+		// Assembly is done, compress the matrix
+		Base::finalize();
+	}
+
+
+} // namespace gismo
+
+
+#ifndef GISMO_BUILD_LIB
+#include GISMO_HPP_HEADER(gsPoissonAssembler.hpp)
+#endif

defect: The new elementInSupportOf indexes the d x 2 support matrix as sup(0,i)/sup(1,i) (transposed) and takes the max instead of the min for the upper corner, so the box intersection is wrong.
In the new elementInSupportOf, the box intersection takes the maximum for the upper corner where it needs the minimum (`>=` instead of `<=`), and it indexes sup(0,i)/sup(1,i) in the wrong order.
std::max(T, double) with std::pow(10.0, ...) cannot deduce a single type when T is not double (for example long double), so it fails to compile.

defect: The new coefficient scaling sums both patch coefficients into one field and uses (sum-rho_k)/rho_k, which gives the inverted weight rho_k/(rho_k+rho_j) and breaks at corners where more than two patches meet.

The new coefficient scaling adds (sum of the other coefficients)/coef[k] instead of coef[k]/coef[neighbour], so the jumps get the inverted rho-scaling (weighted by the patch's own coefficient), and the per-row sum breaks with corner primals.

helper() uses 0 as both the 'unset' sentinel and a valid (patch, local index), and sizes 'which' by the global patchSize while indexing it by local free indices, so entries can go out of bounds or map wrong.

helper() uses 0 both as the 'unset' sentinel and as a valid local index. It also sizes 'which' by the global patch size while indexing it with the other patch's local-mapper index, which mixes index spaces and can give wrong or out-of-range constraints.

The commit moved the explicit specialization gsXml<gsOptionList> from the header into the .cpp. Other translation units (for example gsCmdLine.h calling gsXml<gsOptionList>::get_into) then see the primary template, so the build breaks.

The header renames the ratio() declarations to namespace `utils` while gsBenchmark.cpp still defines them in namespace `benchmark`, so utils::ratio has no definition and linking fails.
np2 is computed as (np.size()>1 ? np(2)-1 : 0), so for 2D grids it reads np(2) out of bounds.
np2 is computed as `np.size()>1 ? np(2)-1 : 0`, which reads out of bounds for 2D grids where np has two entries.

Reading corner values now dereferences child->first_attribute("component") unconditionally, so existing XML <cv> nodes without a component attribute dereference null and crash.

The OpenMP reduction is declared for `struct closestPointHelper` while the variable is `__closestPointHelper`, which fails to compile with OpenMP, and under default(shared) `tmp` is shared across threads, which is a data race.

Removing const from the input parameter of eval_into(gsMatrix<T>& u, ...) means it no longer overrides gsFunction::eval_into(const gsMatrix<T>&, ...); it becomes a hiding overload and virtual dispatch skips it.
The new filter in get() tests `c->m_unkcomp == -1` instead of `comp == -1`, so the default call (comp=-1, meaning all components) drops every component-specific condition.
get() adds comp=-1 as 'all components' but filters with `c->m_unkcomp == comp || c->m_unkcomp == -1`, so the default call drops every component-specific BC.

defect: The new expr+scalar operators build add_expr<_expr<Scalar>,E> but pass the operands in the wrong order, and they use the non-constant _expr<Scalar> instead of _expr<Scalar,true>, so the operator is ill-typed.

geoMap2vtk writes point coordinates with loops bounded by n, the number of patches, instead of pts.rows(), the coordinate dimension, which gives wrong or out-of-range output.

The new gsField toVTK builds its grid from field.fields().basis(i).support(); through a gsFunctionSet reference, basis(i) static_casts piece(i) to gsBasis, which is wrong or asserts for multipatch and non-spline fields.

The new addLevel maps every new knot in a span to dirIndices[i]+1, so several knots inserted into one knot span get duplicate or wrong level indices. It also leaves gsDebugVar output in.

elementInSupportOf is added as a second, identical member declaration in gsRationalBasis (one already exists at line 148), which is a redeclaration compile error.
deriv2Single_into tests isTruncated(i) instead of !isTruncated(i), so the condition is inverted and truncated functions take the plain tensor branch.
deriv2Single_into replaced `m_is_truncated[i] == -1` with `isTruncated(i)` instead of `!isTruncated(i)`, which inverts the branch, so truncated functions take the plain tensor-basis path.
next() calls nextLeaf() when nextLexicographic succeeded instead of when it failed, so the iterator skips elements and leaves.
